actions.justification: Mandatory first step to formally assess and document vital signs. Patient has HR 96, BP 158/94, SpO2 97% — hemodynamically stable but needs formal assessment to guide subsequent management.

Mandatory — required to confirm AF diagnosis and assess for accessory pathways, ischemia, or other findings. Also required BEFORE any rate control per ESC guideline (rate control without ECG is contraindicated).

Mandatory — patient has multiple high-risk features (prior stroke/TIA, HFrEF, HTN, DM) giving a very high CHA2DS2-VASc score, making anticoagulation highly likely to be indicated. Must be formally assessed.

Mandatory lab — assess electrolytes (K+, Mg), renal function, and glucose before initiating rate control therapy in this patient with hypertension, DM, and HFrEF. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.

Mandatory lab — thyroid dysfunction is a reversible cause of AF. TSH assessment is required per ESC AF guidelines, especially before any antiarrhythmic therapy consideration. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.

Patient has AF with multiple high-risk comorbidities (prior stroke/TIA, HFrEF, hypertension, DM). Continuous cardiac monitoring is essential to track rate response and detect hemodynamic deterioration while workup proceeds.

Mandatory per ESC AF guidelines. This patient has multiple stroke risk factors (prior stroke/TIA, hypertension, diabetes, HFrEF) giving a very high CHA2DS2-VASc score, making anticoagulation assessment critical and urgent.

Rate control is recommended as initial strategy for stable AF per ESC guidelines. HR is 96 with HFrEF present — beta blocker (e.g., metoprolol) is appropriate for rate control in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. ECG has already been obtained, so rate control without ECG is not an issue.

Patient has complex comorbidities (HFrEF, prior stroke/TIA, hypertension, diabetes) with new AF — cardiology consultation is warranted to guide ongoing rate vs. rhythm control strategy and anticoagulation management.

Guidelines explicitly state rate control must NOT be given without ECG confirmation. While a 12-lead ECG was obtained, ordering a follow-up ECG documents current rhythm before proceeding to rate control medications, ensuring guideline compliance and safety.

ESC AF guidelines mandate rate control as the initial strategy for stable AF. Patient has HR 96 with palpitations and dyspnea. ECG has been obtained, CHA2DS2-VASc assessed, and anticoagulation need evaluated — prerequisites are met. Rate control is now indicated.

This patient has hypertension, T2DM, HFrEF, and prior stroke/TIA — a very high CHA2DS2-VASc score (≥4). ESC guidelines strongly recommend anticoagulation to reduce stroke risk. Anticoagulation need has been assessed; initiation is now appropriate.
Chest X-ray is indicated to evaluate for pulmonary congestion, cardiomegaly, or other structural causes contributing to AF and dyspnea, especially given the patient's HFrEF comorbidity.

Echocardiogram is essential to assess left ventricular function, left atrial size, valvular disease, and thrombus risk in this patient with HFrEF and prior stroke/TIA, which will guide further AF management.

Electrophysiology consultation is warranted given the patient's complex comorbidities (prior stroke/TIA, HFrEF, hypertension, diabetes) to guide long-term rhythm vs. rate control strategy and optimize antiarrhythmic therapy.
CBC is important to assess for anemia (which can exacerbate AF and dyspnea) and to evaluate baseline hematologic status before anticoagulation therapy in this high-risk patient with prior stroke/TIA.
Renal function assessment is critical for anticoagulant dosing (especially NOACs) and for evaluating comorbid kidney disease in this patient with hypertension, diabetes, and heart failure.

Coagulation studies (PT/INR) are essential to establish baseline clotting status and to guide anticoagulation management in this patient with high CHA2DS2-VASc score (prior stroke, HFrEF, HTN, DM, age).

Patient has received anticoagulation and has prior stroke/TIA with high CHA2DS2-VASc score. INR monitoring is essential to assess anticoagulation adequacy and guide ongoing therapy, particularly if warfarin is being used.
Patient has known HFrEF as a comorbidity. NT-proBNP measurement is indicated to assess current heart failure status, which may influence AF management strategy and guide treatment decisions.

This patient with AF, HFrEF, hypertension, and diabetes warrants troponin measurement to assess for myocardial injury or ischemia as a precipitant or consequence of AF, which has not yet been ordered.

Echocardiogram is indicated to evaluate left ventricular function, valvular disease, and left atrial size in this patient with HFrEF and AF, which is clinically distinct from the imaging_echocardiogram already completed and important for guiding rhythm vs. rate control strategy.

This patient has a high CHA2DS2-VASc score (prior stroke/TIA, HFrEF, hypertension, diabetes, age factors) and anticoagulation need has been assessed. Heparin bridging is indicated to ensure continuous anticoagulant coverage while oral anticoagulation (already initiated) takes effect, particularly given the prior stroke/TIA history.

Digoxin is a reasonable adjunct for rate control in AF patients with HFrEF, particularly when beta-blockers alone may not achieve adequate rate control. The patient has heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, making digoxin a guideline-supported option for rate control in this context.
